steps.description: Attacker discovers that the proxy's upgrade function lacks proper access control. The upgradeToAndCall function is externally callable by anyone, missing the critical onlyAdmin modifier that should restrict it to the proxy admin.

The proxy writes the attacker's malicious implementation address into the EIP-1967 implementation storage slot (0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc). All future delegatecalls from the proxy will now execute the attacker's code.

The malicious implementation includes a drain function disguised as an initializer. Since delegatecall executes in the proxy's storage context, the attacker's code can access and manipulate all funds held by the proxy contract.

Attacker calls the drain function on the proxy, which delegatecalls to the malicious implementation. Since the proxy holds all protocol funds, the attacker transfers every token balance to their wallet. Multiple tokens are drained in sequence.

Attacker launders the stolen funds through mixing protocols and cross-chain bridges to obscure the trail. The protocol is left with an empty proxy pointing to malicious code. Recovery requires a new deployment and is typically impossible for the stolen funds.
